answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a small refundable stake that is locked per identity and slashed on proven fraud — like a terrace garden where each plot needs a deposit before planting. A lone comet of new fake accounts cannot afford thousands of deposits, while honest agents earn theirs back through attested work. Reputation then grows slowly over time, so a fresh identity starts in the tundra: cold, barren, and untrusted until it has proven useful work.
